• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "dither_floyd_steinberg", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Error-diffusion dithering (Floyd–Steinberg). a is the bit count 1 to 8; b is unused.

After rounding each pixel, it distributes the resulting error: 7/16 to the right, 3/16 to the lower left, 5/16 below, 1/16 to the lower right. The mean is preserved (additions and subtractions balance locally), so flat gradations are rendered as dot density instead of stripes. This is why the picture stays readable even when reduced to 1 bit.

Conditions of use: (1) It depends on the scan order, so changing the position where the image is cropped changes the result — unsuitable for tile processing or parallelisation (use dither_ordered for that). (2) Because it sends the error to its neighbours, it leaves tails around thin lines. (3) This is a plain sequential implementation, so on large images it is much slower than dither_ordered.
